why: Inner width 11 cm gives 16 cm overall; with 1.0 cm steering sigma at full duty it fits the 20 cm opening offset +2 cm. Six AA cells (14.4 Wh, 12.2 Wh usable, 4 extra cells on hand, free) vs ~5.7 Wh needed at 0.49 kg (resistive term rises from ~1.14 to ~1.47 J/m). No catalogue swap is needed since both ranges contain the fix.
No bump_switch parameter changes the 0 m range. HC-SR04 ranges 2 m in any light (10x body length), so the corridor can be driven near full speed: 11 m in ~12-20 s, well under 45 s. $2.50, 2 days.

No wheels4 value can fix these. A wheel never climbs more than its radius, and at most 4.5 cm is less than the 5.45 cm edge. A 9 cm wheel diameter is still narrower than the 9.1 cm trench. A rocker-bogie big enough for the step (r=6) stands about 14 cm and breaks under_sofa (9 cm). Tracks fix all three mechanisms. (1) Porch: an idler at 6.5 cm is above the 5.45 cm edge. (2) Garden: 0.45 x 24 cm = 10.8 cm of support, more than the 9.1 cm trench. (3) Sandbox: two long patches give roughly 100-150 cm2 of contact at about 0.7 kg, so about 0.5-0.7 kPa and under 1 cm of sinkage, below the 2 cm belly. Last time this was refused because the tub was too short for the track. Now the track is 24 cm and the tub is 24 cm, which is inside the allowed tub length of track length ±4 cm. Height is the idler at 6.5 cm plus 1.5 cm of track, so 8.0 cm, under the 9.0 cm sofa. Inner width drops to 10 cm to keep margin in the 20 cm bedroom door. Two things threaten the lawn survey: tracks roll harder, and the 1.8 cm sprocket cuts top speed to about 0.56 m/s at 100:1, so electronics cost about 4.6 J/m. That is about 7-9 J/m, or 35-45 kJ for 5 km, against only 44 kJ usable from the NiMH pack. So the battery moves to Li-ion at 28.2 Wh (3 cells, 138 g, lighter than the 162 g of NiMH), which roughly doubles the energy. The 100:1 N20 motors are kept: two motors on 1.8 cm sprockets give about 13 N at the ground, against about 3 N needed on the 22° ramp. The 5000 m at about 0.5 m/s takes about 10,000 s, under the 14,400 s limit. Cost: track kit $14, 3 cells at $4.5 plus a BMS at $1.5, so $29.00 in all, 4 days lead time, about 57 g of track print plus a tub reprint.
